key_insight: Combining plasma DNA fragmentomics with glycoprotein biomarkers distinguished malignant from benign pancreatic cystic neoplasms with an AUROC of 0.92.
clinical_relevance: This diagnostic biomarker approach—not a drug discovery study—could help refine selection for endoscopic ultrasound, pending further validation.
method: Performed whole-genome sequencing of pretreatment plasma DNA from 341 participants.
Trained and validated a machine-learning fragmentomics model using 121 pancreatic cancer patients and 121 matched healthy controls.
Independently evaluated 99 patients with pancreatic cystic neoplasms, comparing and combining fragmentomics with glycoprotein biomarkers.
evidence_signal: Among 99 cyst patients, 11 had malignant disease during 24.6 months of follow-up; combined biomarkers achieved 91% sensitivity, 88% specificity, 99% negative predictive value and 48% positive predictive value.
watch_item: Only 11 malignant cyst cases were evaluated in an endoscopic-ultrasound referral cohort, limiting precision and generalizability to broader screening populations.
paper_title: Plasma DNA fragmentomic analysis for evaluation of patients with pancreatic cystic neoplasms
